title: Strip 44-byte RIFF headers in StreamingPcmPlayer before audio sample decoding

violation.problem: StreamingPcmPlayer.append feeds incoming byte chunks directly into 16-bit PCM sample buffers without checking for RIFF/WAVE container headers. When unary or headed TTS chunks arrive, ASCII header bytes are decoded as loud 0.57 amplitude audio pops and shift the timeline by 22 samples.
violation.expectedSolution: Detect RIFF magic header bytes at offset 0 of incoming buffers in StreamingPcmPlayer.append() and strip the 44-byte container header before converting PCM bytes to float32 samples.

steps: In studio/src/lib/pcm-player.ts, in StreamingPcmPlayer.append(), inspect the first 4 bytes of incoming pcm.
If the first 4 bytes match ASCII RIFF and length is at least 44, strip the 44-byte header before decoding samples.
Ensure this.sampleCount only increments by raw PCM sample count, with zero samples added for standalone header chunks.
reviewChecklist: StreamingPcmPlayer.append() strips 44-byte RIFF headers without throwing on short chunks
Raw PCM chunks without headers continue to append with zero regression
Carry byte logic for odd PCM frames functions correctly after header stripping
